All 88 candidate rows (sources.csv 56 + sinks.csv 32) were dispositioned; 8 sink rows merged (the sql_format_call construction nodes at postgres_cluster_driver.py:22/:24/:36/:37/:38/:41/:65/:75 into the execute entry of the same SQL statement), yielding 80 label entries.

Labeling performed in-session by the agent's underlying LLM (glm-5.3); 4 batches (batch-1 management_resources.py 19 rows; batch-2 postgres_cluster backend+driver 25 rows; batch-3 docker/configuration/exceptions/prometheus 12 rows; batch-4 all sinks 32 rows); no external LLM API calls.

classification semantics: tp = confirmed genuine for the assigned role in this pass; fp = candidate rejected; candidate = plausible but unresolved, human review requested (kept for conservative recall); unknown = unused this run. API-label tp does NOT equal vulnerability ground-truth TP.

Signature flow_kind values follow labels_schema.json: extraction families map as http_request/db_content/config_file/config_load -> return, route_param/api_param/wrapper_param/cli -> param, internal_transfer -> argument, DBInstance constructor kwargs -> field, orm_query -> unknown (rejected entries).

No sanitizer entries: no DB-API bound parameters exist anywhere in the driver (no execute call passes a second argument); reqparse type=str is type coercion only; get_normalized_username (driver :56-57) splits at '@' and is not a SQL sanitizer; the double-quote quoting in the GRANT/DROP templates (:38/:65/:75) is partial identifier quoting that a '"' in the value breaks out of; the CREATE USER/CREATE DATABASE templates (:36/:41) interpolate raw unquoted values.

Global deployment precondition documented per-entry: the SQL channel exists only under the pg_cluster backend (BACKENDS dict, backends/__init__.py:4, default docker); this operator choice does not by itself demote entries.

Second-order delete path: POST-persisted meta-DB values (entity.db_name/entity.username) reach DROP DATABASE/DROP USER; the source-role entries on that path are kept as candidate pending human confirmation of the DB-content-as-source threat model.
No PyVul ground truth, CVE descriptions, fix commits or external security advisories were consulted; the source tree, CodeQL databases and Augur installation were not modified.
